alignments.note: Finite verb takes its English subject pronoun and lexical verb under rule 17; head on the lexical verb.

`רָחֲקוּ` rendered *they stand aloof*; the subject pronoun stays with the verb under rule 17. Head corrected to *aloof* by rule 44's subtraction test: dropping *aloof* leaves *they stand from me*, which says nothing of distance, while *aloof* alone carries רָחַק's lexeme of being far. *stand* is the competing reading and was rejected, since rule 44 forbids reading rule 24's *lexical predicate* as a preference for the English verb, and *aloof* is a complement rather than a bare particle like *forth* or *away*.
Suffix realized by *me* under rule 18; the lemma displayed on this segment is a distribution defect and the morphology governs (rule 39).

The ASV recasts `מִפָּנַי לֹא־חָשְׂכוּ רֹק` as *spare not to spit in my face*, writing *in* for the preposition's own relation; each morpheme of the phrase has a rendering of its own, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet and rule 2 splits the pair. The margin *Or, at the sight of me* was read and set aside under rule 38.
Possessive suffix realized by *my* under rule 18.
Negative takes the written *not*, which the ASV postposes after the verb (rule 25).
`חָשְׂכוּ` rendered *spare*; the ASV writes no subject pronoun for it here.

The noun `רֹק` is recast as the verbal complement *to spit*; English writes no bare infinitive complement, so the marker *to* is licensed by that rendering and joins the unit under rule 52's closing sentence, headed on the word carrying the lexeme.

review_notes: Head of the `רָחֲקוּ` unit moved from *stand* to *aloof*: the accepted note claimed *stand* carries the verb's lexeme of distancing, but rule 44's subtraction shows the reverse — *stand* alone names posture, *aloof* alone names distance. Everything else in the verse is unchanged.

ASV *spit in my face* recasts the Hebrew *they have not withheld spittle from my face*; the preposition, the noun and the suffix each keep a written English word, so the phrase is split rather than fused under rule 30, unlike the מִפָּנַי of JOB.30.11.
Marginal note *Or, at the sight of me* read and set aside under rule 38; the printed text governs.
